weeks.title: Time series I: decomposition, moving averages and exponential smoothing
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki sales jaisi time series ko trend, seasonality aur irregular components me kaise todte hain, additive aur multiplicative models me kaise chunte hain, centred moving average se seasonal indices kaise nikaalte hain, aur simple exponential smoothing aur Holt's method se forecast kaise banate hain.
concepts: **Components**: **trend** (lambi avadhi ki disha, jaise har saal 8% growth), **seasonality** (fixed period pe repeat hone wala pattern: garmi me ice-cream, Diwali pe electronics), **cyclical** (business cycle jaise bina fixed period ke ups-downs) aur **irregular** (random noise, ek-baar ki strike). Forecast se pehle plot dekho aur pehchano ki kaunse components hain.

**Additive vs multiplicative**: additive: Y = T + S + I, jab seasonal swing ka size level badhne pe bhi lagbhag same rahe (har December +200 units). Multiplicative: Y = T × S × I, jab swing level ke proportion me bade (har December +25%). Growing business me aksar multiplicative fit hota hai; log lene se multiplicative additive ban jaata hai.

**Moving averages**: m-period trailing MA = pichhle m values ka average; simple forecast ke roop me next value = last m ka average. Centred MA trend nikaalta hai aur seasonality ko smooth kar deta hai jab m = season length. Even period (jaise 4 quarters) me 4-MA do quarters ke beech pe baithta hai, isliye do consecutive 4-MAs ka average lete hain: **2×4 centred MA**.

**Seasonal indices (ratio-to-moving-average)**: multiplicative model me har quarter ke liye ratio = actual / centred MA. Same quarter ke ratios ka average lo, phir indices ko scale karo taaki unka average 1 ho (4 quarters ka sum 4). **Deseasonalised value** = actual / index; isse 'Q4 me sales giri ya bas season tha' pata chalta hai.

**Simple exponential smoothing (SES)**: Fₜ₊₁ = α·yₜ + (1 − α)·Fₜ, 0 < α ≤ 1. Equivalent: naya forecast = purana forecast + α × (error). Weights exponentially girte hain: k periods purane observation ka weight α(1 − α)^k. Bada α ⇒ tez reaction par noisy; chhota α ⇒ smooth par slow. SES sirf level ke liye hai, trend ya seasonality wali series pe yeh lag karega.

**Holt's linear trend method**: level Lₜ = α·yₜ + (1 − α)(Lₜ₋₁ + Tₜ₋₁); trend Tₜ = β·(Lₜ − Lₜ₋₁) + (1 − β)·Tₜ₋₁; h-step forecast Fₜ₊ₕ = Lₜ + h·Tₜ. **Holt–Winters** isme seasonal component jodta hai (additive ya multiplicative). α, β ko aam taur pe historical one-step errors minimise karke chunte hain.

**Benchmarks pehle**: naive (agla = last value), seasonal naive (agla Q4 = pichhla Q4) aur moving average hamesha compute karo. Complex model in benchmarks ko out-of-sample nahi hara paata toh use deploy karne ka koi fayda nahi.

example.problem: Himalaya Creamery (fictional) ki quarterly sales (₹ lakh): 2023: Q1 40, Q2 70, Q3 60, Q4 30; 2024: Q1 48, Q2 82, Q3 68, Q4 38. 2×4 centred moving averages aur multiplicative seasonal ratios nikaalo, aur normalised seasonal indices batao.
steps: 4-quarter MAs: (40 + 70 + 60 + 30) / 4 = 50; phir 52, 55, 57, 59 (har baar ek quarter aage).
Centred MAs (do consecutive 4-MAs ka average): Q3-2023 = (50 + 52) / 2 = 51; Q4-2023 = 53.5; Q1-2024 = 56; Q2-2024 = 58.
Ratios ka sum ≈ 4.008, toh har ratio ko 4 / 4.008 se multiply karke normalise karo.
Interpretation: Q2 (garmi) me sales trend se lagbhag 41% upar, Q4 me lagbhag 44% neeche. Q4-2024 ki 38 ko deseasonalise karo: 38 / 0.560 ≈ 67.9, jo trend ke saath consistent hai.

mistakes: Even period ke liye simple 4-MA ko kisi ek quarter ka trend maan lena. Fix: 4-MA do quarters ke beech pe hota hai; 2×4 centred MA lo.
Trend wali series pe SES lagana aur hairaan hona ki forecast hamesha peeche reh jaata hai. Fix: trend ho toh Holt, seasonality bhi ho toh Holt–Winters.
Seasonal indices normalise na karna. Fix: multiplicative indices ka average 1 (sum = season length) aur additive indices ka sum 0 hona chahiye.
revision: Y = T + S + I (additive) ya T × S × I (multiplicative).
Swing level ke saath bade ⇒ multiplicative.
Even season ⇒ 2×4 centred MA.
Seasonal index = avg(actual / CMA), normalised; deseasonalised = actual / index.
SES: Fₜ₊₁ = αyₜ + (1 − α)Fₜ.
Holt: Fₜ₊ₕ = Lₜ + h·Tₜ.

questions.question: Ek e-commerce company ki monthly sales har saal lagbhag 30% badhti hai, aur festive season ka spike bhi har saal bada hota jaata hai: pehle saal +₹2 crore, teesre saal +₹3.4 crore, jabki spike hamesha usi saal ki baseline ka lagbhag 40% rehta hai. Kaunsa decomposition model zyada suitable hai?
options: Additive, kyunki seasonal spike har saal aata hai
Sirf trend model, seasonality ignore karo
Multiplicative, kyunki seasonal swing level ke proportion me badh raha hai
Additive, kyunki trend linear hai
questions.explanation: Spike ka absolute size badh raha hai par level ka constant share (~40%) hai, yaani S level ko multiply karta hai: multiplicative model, option C. Trap: option A sirf 'pattern repeat hota hai' dekhta hai; additive model tab hota jab spike rupees me lagbhag constant rehta. Option D bhi galat hai: trend 30% compounding hai (linear nahi), aur additive/multiplicative ka chunaav seasonal swing ke size se hota hai.

questions.question: Ek kirana distributor ki weekly sales (₹ hazaar): 120, 135, 126, 141. 3-week trailing moving average se agle hafte ka forecast kya hai?
questions.explanation: Last 3 weeks: (135 + 126 + 141) / 3 = 402 / 3 = 134, option A. Trap: option B chaaron weeks ka average hai (4-week MA); option C naive forecast (sirf last value) hai; option D pehle teen weeks (120, 135, 126) ka average hai, jo latest week ko ignore kar deta hai.

questions.question: SES with α = 0.3. Month 1 ka forecast F₁ = 100 tha. Actual demand: month 1 = 110, month 2 = 90. Month 3 ka forecast F₃ kya hai?
questions.explanation: F₂ = 0.3 × 110 + 0.7 × 100 = 103. F₃ = 0.3 × 90 + 0.7 × 103 = 27 + 72.1 = 99.1, option B. Trap: option C F₂ ko update kiye bina purana F₁ = 100 use karta hai (0.3 × 90 + 0.7 × 100 = 97); option A sirf F₂ hai; option D weights ulte laga deta hai (0.7 × 90 + 0.3 × 103).

questions.question: Ek electronics retailer ki Q4 sales ₹130 crore hai aur multiplicative model me Q4 ka seasonal index 1.30 hai. Deseasonalised Q4 sales kya hai?
options: ₹169 crore
₹128.7 crore
₹130 crore
₹100 crore
questions.explanation: Multiplicative model me deseasonalised = actual / index = 130 / 1.30 = ₹100 crore, option D: season ka 30% boost hata diya. Trap: option A index se divide karne ki jagah multiply karta hai; option B additive soch ke 1.30 ghatata hai (index ek ratio hai, rupees nahi); option C seasonality adjust hi nahi karta.

questions.question: Quarterly sales: Q1 = 20, Q2 = 30, Q3 = 40, Q4 = 26, agle saal Q1 = 24. Q3 pe 2×4 centred moving average kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehla 4-MA (Q1–Q4) = 116 / 4 = 29, jo Q2 aur Q3 ke beech baithta hai; doosra 4-MA (Q2–agla Q1) = 120 / 4 = 30, jo Q3 aur Q4 ke beech hai. Centred MA at Q3 = (29 + 30) / 2 = 29.5, option A. Trap: options B aur C sirf ek 4-MA lete hain, jo exactly Q3 pe centred nahi hai; option D Q2, Q3, Q4 ka 3-point average hai, jo poore season ko smooth nahi karta.

questions.question: Holt's method (Lₜ = αyₜ + (1 − α)(Lₜ₋₁ + Tₜ₋₁), Tₜ = β(Lₜ − Lₜ₋₁) + (1 − β)Tₜ₋₁, Fₜ₊ₕ = Lₜ + h·Tₜ): pichhla level Lₜ₋₁ = 200, pichhla trend Tₜ₋₁ = 10, naya actual yₜ = 220, α = 0.4, β = 0.5. Lₜ aur Tₜ update karke 3 periods aage ka forecast Fₜ₊₃ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Lₜ = 0.4 × 220 + 0.6 × (200 + 10) = 88 + 126 = 214. Tₜ = 0.5 × (214 − 200) + 0.5 × 10 = 7 + 5 = 12. Fₜ₊₃ = 214 + 3 × 12 = 250, option D. Trap: option A trend update karna bhool jaata hai (214 + 3 × 10); option B level ki jagah actual 220 se start karta hai (220 + 36); option C sirf 2 steps lagata hai (214 + 24).

weeks.title: Time series II: autocorrelation, AR models and forecast accuracy
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki autocorrelation function (ACF) se series ki memory kaise padhte hain, stationarity kyun zaroori hai aur differencing kya karta hai, AR(1) model se multi-step forecast kaise banate hain, aur MAE, RMSE, MAPE se forecasts ko time-ordered holdout pe kaise compare karte hain.
concepts: **Autocorrelation**: series ka apne hi pichhle values ke saath correlation. Lag-k sample autocorrelation: rₖ = Σₜ (yₜ − ȳ)(yₜ₊ₖ − ȳ) / Σₜ (yₜ − ȳ)², jahan numerator me n − k pairs hain aur denominator poori series ka sum of squares. ACF plot har lag k ka rₖ dikhata hai; white noise ke liye lagbhag 95% values ±2 / √n band ke andar honi chahiye.

**ACF patterns padhna**: dheere-dheere girta ACF ⇒ trend / non-stationarity; season length pe spikes (jaise monthly data me lag 12) ⇒ seasonality; sirf lag 1 pe bada aur phir jaldi khatam ⇒ short memory. Model fit karne ke baad residuals ka ACF bhi check karo: koi bada spike bacha hai toh model ne pattern miss kiya (Ljung–Box test is idea ko formal banata hai).

**Stationarity**: series ka mean, variance aur autocorrelation structure time ke saath constant rahe. Stock prices, cumulative downloads, ya trend wali sales stationary nahi hain; daily % returns aur first differences aksar lagbhag stationary hote hain. Zyaadatar classical models (AR, ARMA) stationary series maangte hain, warna spurious regression aur galat forecasts milte hain.

**Differencing aur random walk**: Δyₜ = yₜ − yₜ₋₁ trend hata deta hai; seasonal difference yₜ − yₜ₋₁₂ annual pattern hata deta hai. **Random walk** yₜ = yₜ₋₁ + εₜ non-stationary hai (variance time ke saath badhta hai), par uska first difference white noise hai; iska best forecast simply last value (naive) hai.

**AR(1) model**: yₜ = c + φ·yₜ₋₁ + εₜ, |φ| < 1 ho toh stationary. Long-run mean μ = c / (1 − φ). h-step forecast: ŷₜ₊ₕ = μ + φ^h·(yₜ − μ), yaani forecast exponentially mean ki taraf lautta hai. Theoretical ACF = φ^k (dheere girta), jabki PACF lag 1 ke baad cut off hota hai; AR(p) ke liye PACF lag p ke baad cut off hota hai.

**Forecast error metrics** (eₜ = actual − forecast): **MAE** = mean |e|, same units, outliers pe kam sensitive. **RMSE** = √(mean e²), badi galtiyon ko zyada penalise karta hai; RMSE ≥ MAE hamesha. **MAPE** = mean |e / actual| × 100%, scale-free par actual 0 ke paas ho toh explode karta hai aur under-forecast vs over-forecast ko asymmetric treat karta hai. Metric business cost se chuno.

**Evaluation design**: time series ko shuffle karke split mat karo. Pehle ke data pe fit, baad ke holdout pe test (ya rolling-origin / walk-forward). Hamesha naive ya seasonal-naive benchmark ke saath compare karo; **MASE** = model ka MAE / naive ka in-sample MAE, < 1 matlab naive se behtar.

example.problem: Ek cement dealer (fictional) ki monthly demand (hazaar bags) ke liye fitted model: yₜ = 12 + 0.8·yₜ₋₁ + εₜ. Is mahine demand 66 thi. Long-run mean, agle do mahine ke forecasts, aur model ke theoretical ACF ke pehle do values batao.
steps: |φ| = 0.8 < 1, toh series stationary hai. Long-run mean μ = c / (1 − φ) = 12 / 0.2 = 60.
1-step forecast: ŷ = 12 + 0.8 × 66 = 64.8.
Forecasts 66 se 60 ki taraf lautte hain: har step pe mean se gap 0.8 guna ho jaata hai.
Theoretical ACF: ρ₁ = φ = 0.8, ρ₂ = φ² = 0.64 (dheere girta hai); PACF lag 1 ke baad lagbhag zero hoga.
example.code:
c, phi, y = 12, 0.8, 66
mu = c / (1 - phi)
for h in range(1, 4):
    y = c + phi * y
    print(h, round(y, 3))   # 64.8, 63.84, 63.072
print('long-run mean', round(mu, 2))  # 60.0

mistakes: Trend wali (non-stationary) series pe seedha AR model ya correlation lagana. Fix: pehle plot aur ACF dekho; differencing ya detrending karke stationary banao.
Time series ko random shuffle karke train/test split karna. Fix: time order rakho; future ko kabhi training me leak mat hone do.
Jis series me zero ya bahut chhote actuals hain (jaise slow-moving spare parts) uspe MAPE use karna. Fix: MAE, RMSE ya MASE lo.
revision: rₖ = Σ(yₜ − ȳ)(yₜ₊ₖ − ȳ) / Σ(yₜ − ȳ)²; band ±2/√n.
Stationary: constant mean, variance, autocorrelation.
Random walk ka difference white noise; forecast = last value.
AR(1): μ = c / (1 − φ); ŷₜ₊ₕ = μ + φ^h(yₜ − μ).
MAE robust; RMSE badi galtiyan penalise karta hai; MAPE scale-free.
Time-ordered holdout + naive benchmark.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsi series sabse zyada lagbhag stationary hone ki ummeed hai?
options: Ek stock index ke daily percentage returns
Usi index ka daily closing level
Ek app ke cumulative total downloads
Har saal 40% badhne wale startup ka monthly revenue
questions.explanation: Daily returns ek stable mean (lagbhag 0) ke aas-paas ghoomte hain aur unka koi lasting trend nahi hota, isliye woh lagbhag stationary hain: option A. Trap: option B (index level) random walk jaisa hai, jiska mean aur variance time ke saath badalta hai; returns isi level ka (percentage) difference hain. Options C aur D me clear trend hai.

questions.question: 4 hafton ka actual demand: 50, 60, 40, 50 aur forecast: 45, 62, 46, 50. MAE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Errors (actual − forecast): 5, −2, −6, 0. |e| ka mean = (5 + 2 + 6 + 0) / 4 = 13 / 4 = 3.25, option D. Trap: option A signed errors ka mean (bias) hai, jisme positive aur negative galtiyan cancel ho jaati hain; option B RMSE hai (√(65 / 4)); option C average ki jagah total absolute error hai.

questions.question: 4 SKUs ka actual sale: 200, 250, 100, 50 aur forecast: 170, 250, 110, 60. MAPE kya hai?
questions.explanation: Percentage errors: 30 / 200 = 15%, 0 / 250 = 0%, 10 / 100 = 10%, 10 / 50 = 20%. MAPE = (15 + 0 + 10 + 20) / 4 = 11.25%, option C. Trap: option A total absolute error / total actual (50 / 600) hai, jo WAPE hai, MAPE nahi; option B MAE (12.5 units) ko % likh deta hai; option D average ki jagah sum hai. Dhyan do: 50 wale chhote SKU ka 20% error MAPE pe sabse bhari pada.

questions.question: Ek short series: 2, 4, 6, 8, 6, 4. Standard ACF formula (numerator me 5 lag-1 pairs, denominator me poori series ka Σ(yₜ − ȳ)²) se lag-1 autocorrelation r₁ kya hai?
questions.explanation: ȳ = 30 / 6 = 5; deviations −3, −1, 1, 3, 1, −1. Denominator = 9 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 1 + 1 = 22. Numerator = (−3)(−1) + (−1)(1) + (1)(3) + (3)(1) + (1)(−1) = 3 − 1 + 3 + 3 − 1 = 7. r₁ = 7 / 22 ≈ 0.318, option B. Trap: option A pairs (yₜ, yₜ₊₁) pe alag-alag means ke saath ordinary Pearson correlation hai, jo ACF formula nahi; option C numerator ko 5 aur denominator ko 6 se divide karke 'averages' ka ratio leta hai.

questions.question: 4-month holdout pe actual demand: 100, 120, 80, 100. Model A forecasts: 110, 110, 90, 90. Model B forecasts: 100, 120, 80, 130. Ek badi galti (stock-out ya dead stock) bahut mehngi padti hai, chhoti galtiyan sasti. Kaunsa model chunna chahiye?
options: Model B, kyunki uska MAE (7.5) Model A ke MAE (10) se kam hai
Model B, kyunki uske 4 me se 3 forecasts bilkul exact hain
Model A: MAE me B aage hai (7.5 vs 10), par RMSE me A aage hai (10 vs 15), aur badi galtiyan mehngi hain
Dono barabar hain, kyunki dono ka RMSE 10 hai
questions.explanation: A ke errors: −10, 10, −10, 10 ⇒ MAE = 10, RMSE = 10. B ke errors: 0, 0, 0, −30 ⇒ MAE = 7.5, RMSE = √(900 / 4) = 15. RMSE badi galtiyon ko square karke zyada penalise karta hai, aur yahan badi galti hi mehngi hai, isliye option C. Trap: option A sirf MAE dekhta hai, jo ek 30-unit miss ko teen chhoti galtiyon jaisa hi treat karta hai; option D B ka RMSE galat calculate karta hai.

questions.question: Ek AR(1) model: yₜ = 20 + 0.6·yₜ₋₁ + εₜ. Aaj ki value yₜ = 70 hai. 3 periods aage ka forecast ŷₜ₊₃ kya hai?
questions.explanation: μ = 20 / (1 − 0.6) = 50. ŷₜ₊₃ = μ + φ³(yₜ − μ) = 50 + 0.216 × 20 = 54.32, option B. Step-by-step bhi: 62 → 57.2 → 54.32. Trap: option A sirf 1-step forecast hai; option C seedha long-run mean le leta hai (yeh h → ∞ pe hota hai); option D 0.6³ × 70 leta hai aur constant c bhool jaata hai.

weeks.title: From question to decision: choosing methods, communicating results, data ethics
weeks.summary: Is week aap poore course ko ek case me jodoge: business question ko decision aur KPI me badalna, outcome aur predictor ke type se sahi analysis chunna, statistical result ko break-even aur expected value se decision me badalna, multiple testing ke trap se bachna, results ko manager ke liye saaf communicate karna, aur data privacy aur fairness ka dhyan rakhna.
concepts: **Decision se shuru karo**: 'data me kya hai?' nahi, 'kaunsa decision lena hai aur kis evidence se woh badlega?' Pehle likho: decision options (rollout / na karo / aur test karo), primary KPI, minimum effect jo business ke liye maayne rakhta hai, aur analysis plan. Data dekhne se pehle plan likhna baad me cherry-picking se bachaata hai.

**Method chunna (outcome × predictor)**: categorical outcome vs categorical group → chi-square test (week 3). Numeric outcome, 2 independent groups → Welch t; 3+ groups → one-way ANOVA (week 4). Numeric outcome, numeric / mixed predictors → multiple regression with dummies aur interactions (weeks 5–7). Binary outcome → logistic regression (week 8). Same units baar-baar measure → paired t / RM-ANOVA (week 9). Time-ordered data aur forecast → decomposition, smoothing, AR (weeks 10–11).

**Experiment vs observational data**: randomised experiment (A/B test) me groups average me har cheez me same hote hain, isliye farq ko cause bol sakte ho. Observational data me confounders hote hain (Simpson's paradox, OVB); regression controls madad karte hain par sirf measured confounders ke liye. Jahan possible ho, randomise karo, ya kam se kam ek control group rakho.

**Statistical se business significance tak**: p-value sirf batata hai ki effect zero se alag hai ya nahi. Decision ke liye effect ka **confidence interval** business units me badlo aur **break-even** se compare karo. Poora CI break-even se upar ⇒ rollout; poora neeche ⇒ mat karo; CI break-even ko cross kare ⇒ test badhao ya staged rollout karo.

**Multiple testing aur p-hacking**: 20 segments ya 20 metrics α = 0.05 pe test kiye aur asal me koi effect nahi, toh bhi average me 20 × 0.05 = 1 false positive milega. Primary metric pehle se fix karo, Bonferroni (α / m) jaisa correction lagao, aur 'jo significant mila wahi story' (HARKing) se bacho; exploratory findings ko naye data pe confirm karo.

**Communication**: pehli line me answer aur recommendation ('Rollout 50% traffic pe; expected +₹1 lakh / month, par risk hai'), phir evidence: effect size + uncertainty business units me, ek chart ek message, assumptions aur limitations, aur next step. Jargon (p, F, β) appendix me rakho; manager ko 'kitna, kitna pakka, aur kya karein' chahiye.

**Data ethics aur privacy**: India ka Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 consent, purpose limitation aur data minimisation jaise principles pe khada hai: jis kaam ke liye data liya, usi ke liye use karo, aur zaroorat se zyada mat rakho. Pseudonymised data bhi doosre datasets ke saath jodne pe re-identify ho sakta hai; access control aur aggregation se risk kam karo.

**Fairness aur proxies**: model me gender ya religion na ho tab bhi pincode, name, ya device type unke **proxy** ban sakte hain aur kuch groups ke saath systematically galat decisions ho sakte hain (disparate impact). Group-wise approval rates aur error rates (FPR, FNR) compare karo, proxy features ka justification likho, aur high-stakes decisions (credit, hiring) me human review aur appeal ka raasta rakho.

example.problem: Ganga Foods (fictional) ne naya product page A/B test kiya: control 20,000 visitors pe 4.0% conversion, naya page 20,000 visitors pe 4.4%. Naye page ki monthly cost ₹2,00,000 hai, site pe 5,00,000 visitors / month aate hain, aur har order pe margin ₹150 hai. Kya rollout karna chahiye?
steps: Break-even lift = monthly cost / (visitors × margin) = 2,00,000 / (5,00,000 × 150) ≈ 0.00267 = 0.27 pp.
Point estimate 0.4 pp pe: extra orders = 5,00,000 × 0.004 = 2,000 ⇒ gain ₹3,00,000 − cost ₹2,00,000 = +₹1,00,000 / month.
CI ka lower end (≈ 0.01 pp) break-even se neeche hai, toh 'significant' hone ke bawajood loss ka real chance hai.
Recommendation: staged rollout (jaise 50% traffic) aur 2–4 hafte aur data; agar updated CI ka lower end 0.27 pp se upar aaye toh full rollout.

**Answer**: lift **significant (z ≈ 1.99)** aur expected profit **+₹1 lakh / month**, par CI **(0.01, 0.79) pp** break-even **0.27 pp** ko cross karta hai ⇒ **staged rollout + aur testing**, seedha full rollout nahi.

mistakes: 'p < 0.05' ko hi rollout decision bana dena. Fix: effect ka CI business units me nikaalo aur break-even / cost se compare karo.
Bahut saare segments test karke sirf significant wale report karna. Fix: primary metric pehle fix karo, multiple-testing correction lagao, aur sab tests report karo.
Sensitive attribute hata ke model ko 'fair' maan lena. Fix: proxies dhoondo aur group-wise approval aur error rates check karo.
revision: Decision → KPI → minimum useful effect → method → data.
Categorical × categorical → χ²; numeric × groups → t / ANOVA; binary → logistic.
Same units repeated → paired / RM; time order → TS methods.
CI vs break-even: decision isi se lo, sirf p se nahi.
m tests ⇒ ~m × α false positives; Bonferroni α / m.
DPDP Act 2023: consent, purpose limitation, minimisation; proxies se fairness check.

questions.question: Ek beverage company jaanna chahti hai ki teen age groups (18–25, 26–40, 41+) ke 600 respondents ka favourite flavour (Mango / Lemon / Cola) age group pe depend karta hai ya nahi. Kaunsa analysis sahi hai?
options: One-way ANOVA
Logistic regression with a numeric outcome
Paired t-test
Chi-square test of independence
questions.explanation: Outcome (flavour) aur group (age band) dono categorical hain, aur sawaal association ka hai: 3 × 3 contingency table pe chi-square test of independence, option D. Trap: option A tab hota jab outcome numeric hota (jaise rating ya spend); option C same logon ke do measurements ke liye hai.

questions.question: Ek NBFC naye applicants ke liye predict karna chahti hai ki woh 12 mahine me default karenge (haan / nahi), income, existing EMIs aur credit history ke basis pe, aur har applicant ke liye default probability chahiye. Kaunsa method sabse suitable hai?
options: Simple linear regression
Logistic regression
Chi-square goodness-of-fit test
Simple exponential smoothing
questions.explanation: Outcome binary hai aur har applicant ki probability chahiye, kai numeric predictors ke saath: logistic regression, option B. Trap: option A linear model 0–1 ke bahar predictions de sakta hai aur binary outcome ke liye bana nahi hai; option D time series forecasting ke liye hai, individual classification ke liye nahi.

questions.question: Ek retail chain ne apne 30 stores me naya store layout lagaya aur har store ki layout se pehle aur baad ki monthly sales record ki. Layout ka effect test karne ke liye sabse sahi approach kya hai?
options: Har store ke (after − before) difference pe paired t-test, aur ideally un stores ka control group bhi jahan layout nahi badla
Before aur after ko 30 + 30 independent stores maan ke Welch two-sample t-test
Chi-square test of independence
Before aur after ko do groups maan ke one-way ANOVA
questions.explanation: Same 30 stores do baar measure hue, toh har store ka difference lo aur paired t-test karo; store-to-store variation hat jaata hai, option A. Control stores isliye chahiye kyunki season ya market trend bhi before/after farq bana sakta hai. Trap: option B aur option D observations ko independent maan lete hain (dono me store-level pairing ignore hoti hai), isliye power kho dete hain; option C categorical data ke liye hai.

questions.question: Ek naye checkout flow ki monthly cost ₹3,00,000 hai. Site pe 8,00,000 visitors / month aate hain aur har order pe margin ₹125 hai. A/B test me conversion lift 0.5 percentage points aaya. Break-even lift kitna hai, aur kya point estimate pe rollout profitable hai?
options: 3.0 pp; nahi, kyunki 0.5 pp < 3.0 pp
0.03 pp; haan, kyunki lift break-even se bahut upar hai
0.30 pp; haan, kyunki 0.5 pp > 0.30 pp (monthly gain ₹5,00,000 vs cost ₹3,00,000)
0.50 pp; break-even wahi hai jo observed lift hai
questions.explanation: Break-even = cost / (visitors × margin) = 3,00,000 / (8,00,000 × 125) = 0.003 = 0.30 pp. 0.5 pp pe extra orders = 8,00,000 × 0.005 = 4,000 ⇒ gain = 4,000 × 125 = ₹5,00,000 > ₹3,00,000, option C. Trap: options A aur B fraction ko percentage points me badalte waqt decimal galat jagah laga dete hain (0.003 = 0.3 pp, na 3 pp na 0.03 pp); option D observed lift ko hi break-even maan leta hai.

questions.question: Ek lending startup ka credit model gender aur religion use nahi karta, par 'pincode' ek strong predictor hai. Audit me dikhta hai ki kuch specific areas ke applicants ka approval rate bahut kam hai, jabki unka actual repayment baaki areas jaisa hai. Sabse sahi response kya hai?
options: Kuch karne ki zaroorat nahi, kyunki model me sensitive attributes hain hi nahi
Pincode proxy discrimination ka source ho sakta hai: group-wise approval aur error rates check karo, pincode ki zaroorat justify karo ya hatao / replace karo, aur human review rakho
Pincode rakho par model ka threshold sabke liye 0.5 kar do
Un areas se applications lena band kar do kyunki model unhe risky maanta hai
questions.explanation: Sensitive attribute hatane se fairness guarantee nahi hoti; pincode income, community ya religion ka proxy ban sakta hai. Jab actual repayment same ho par approval kam ho, toh model un groups pe zyada false positives (achhe applicants reject) de raha hai: option B ka audit-and-fix approach sahi hai. Trap: option A 'fairness through unawareness' ka galat bharosa hai; option C threshold badalne se proxy ka bias nahi jaata.

questions.question: Marketing team ne ek campaign ka effect 20 customer segments me alag-alag test kiya, har test α = 0.05 pe. Do segments significant aaye, p = 0.012 aur p = 0.0018. Agar campaign ka asal me kahin bhi effect nahi hota, toh expected false positives kitne, Bonferroni threshold kya hai, aur kaunse results survive karte hain?
options: Expected 1 false positive; threshold 0.0025; sirf p = 0.0018 wala survive karta hai
Expected 0.05 false positive; threshold 0.05; dono survive karte hain
Expected 1 false positive; threshold 0.0025; dono survive karte hain
Expected 1 false positive; threshold 0.0025; koi survive nahi karta
questions.explanation: Expected false positives = m × α = 20 × 0.05 = 1. Bonferroni threshold = 0.05 / 20 = 0.0025. 0.0018 < 0.0025 survive karta hai, 0.012 > 0.0025 nahi, isliye option A. Trap: option B correction hi nahi lagata aur 20 tests ko ek test jaisa treat karta hai; option C threshold sahi likhta hai par 0.012 ko compare karna bhool jaata hai; option D 0.0018 ko bhi galti se reject kar deta hai.
